name: Ambessa, Matriarch of War
howItPlays: Ambessa becomes empowered any time you empower another card, and while empowered you can pay to ready one of your units so it can attack again in the same turn. You keep your units swinging forward every turn, daring your opponent to find an answer before you hit them twice.
whyYou: You want to be the one asking the questions, not answering them, and you're happy sending your units forward again and again rather than sitting back. You like a deck that peaks early and hits hard, and you don't mind that it can run out of steam if a game drags on, because your plan is to have already won by then. If pressing an advantage the moment you get it sounds more fun than playing patient, Ambessa fits you.
ratingNotes: Ability: when you empower something else, empower me; disempower me + a rainbow rune + Exhaust: ready a unit (Riftcodex, VEN). pace 7.5: riftboundguide says Ambessa 'doesn't scale very well into the late game' and 'her lack of draw makes the Matriarch of War unfit for long, value-oriented matches,' pushing the deck to do its work early. stance 8: riftboundguide states 'Ambessa does not retreat. She presses forward and asks her opponent to answer a unit that just attacked twice.' complexity 5.5: riftbound.gg calls the timing 'moderate complexity with emphasis on unit synergies and proper timing,' and riftboundguide notes you need 'enough Empower density elsewhere on the board to make paying it worthwhile every turn,' a real but not extreme planning demand. variance 5.5: riftboundguide notes 'Ambessa has yet to find its refined build' and that her output depends on 'generating sufficient Empower triggers,' so results vary with the exact build and draw. archetype Aggro: chosen over the seed's Midrange because both sources describe a deck that presses an early advantage and fades late rather than one built to play a long game; the 'does not retreat' framing and weak late-game read as Aggro. Confidence: medium, two guides read, but one explicitly flags the archetype as still unsettled in the metagame, so these numbers may shift as the format matures. starterDeck kept null: neither guide names a confirmed retail starter product for this specific printing, and one search turned up an unconfirmed note that Ambessa's own Champion Deck had not gone on sale separately as of these sources; reviewer should re-check this if a product launches.
